key_concept: The continuity equation $A_1v_1 = A_2v_2$ combined with Bernoulli's equation for a horizontal pipe, $P_1 - P_2 = \tfrac{1}{2}\rho(v_2^2 - v_1^2)$, gives the flow speed and hence the volume flow rate $Q = Av$.
steps: Bernoulli for a horizontal pipe (same height): $P_P - P_Q = \tfrac{1}{2}\rho(v_Q^2 - v_P^2) = \tfrac{1}{2}\rho(4v_P^2 - v_P^2) = \tfrac{3}{2}\rho v_P^2$.
Rate of flow: $Q = A_P v_P = 40\ \text{cm}^2 \times 10\ \text{cm s}^{-1} = 400\ \text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$.
Check at $Q$: $v_Q = 20\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$, so $A_Q v_Q = 20 \times 20 = 400\ \text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$, which is consistent.
why_not_others: 200 results from using the speed at $Q$ with $A_P$ in the wrong combination, or from dropping a factor of 2. 100 and 300 come from unit-conversion slips, or from forgetting the factor $\tfrac{1}{2}$ or the $(4-1)$ term in Bernoulli's equation.
common_trap: Mixing units: you must take $\rho$ in $\text{kg m}^{-3}$ and $\Delta P$ in $\text{N m}^{-2}$, which gives the speed in $\text{m s}^{-1}$, then convert to $\text{cm s}^{-1}$ before multiplying by the area in $\text{cm}^2$.
time_saving_tip: Use the direct formula $Q = A_1A_2\sqrt{\dfrac{2\Delta P}{\rho(A_1^2 - A_2^2)}}$, the venturimeter result. With area ratio 2, $v_P = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\Delta P}{3\rho}} = 0.1\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ instantly.
